title: Crystal Palace Hand Thomas Frank a Rebuild Job
body:
Crystal Palace have made Thomas Frank their new manager [S1]. Nobody in the stands cares who signed the paperwork. They care whether the team stops sliding.

BBC Sport's framing is blunt: it asks whether Frank can rebuild his reputation after a bruising time in charge of Tottenham [S2]. The same coverage treats the job as a rescue mission as much as a fresh start, with the aim of restoring reputation and saving the club [S2]. That is the right way to read it. The new man is taking on a repair job as much as a project.

The recent numbers explain the urgency. Over the last five league matches, Palace have won once, drawn none and lost four, collecting three points [ST1]. They have scored four and conceded thirteen, with the sequence reading WLLLL [ST1]. That is a side that has lost its shape at both ends, and the defensive collapse is where the real damage has been done.

The easy move is always to pull the lever at the top. It fixes nothing on its own. The real test is what comes next, because a rushed replacement can turn one bad spell into a long one.

The Touchline Take: get the next appointment right and this moment is forgotten.
